report.summary: Parsed chunk 2 of docrefs.py: utility functions for reference extraction and resolution, including code block stripping, reference extraction, suffix index building, module file resolution, name collection, and resolve_reference logic.
risks: _strip_code_blocks | medium | Fence detection relies on first three characters; may incorrectly skip lines if fence token is not exactly three characters. | Check if _FENCE regex ensures token is exactly three characters.
_suffix_index | medium | Path suffix mapping may be expensive for large repos; no caching beyond the module. | Consider performance impact.

_collect_names | medium | Star imports and __getattr__ cause dynamic=True; any reference to such module is skipped, potentially missing valid references. | Verify that dynamic modules are correctly identified.

resolve_reference | medium | Anchored detection for dotted names falls back to suffix index if direct module_file returns None; may incorrectly anchor non-anchored references. | Verify the logic for anchored flag.
resolve_reference | low | _by_path uses suffixes.get with lstrip('./') but probe may not have leading './'; may miss some suffix matches. | Confirm usage patterns.
todos: Verify that _FENCE regex matches exactly three characters for fence token.
Test _suffix_index with a sample repository structure.
Test _collect_names with various AST nodes including star imports.
Test resolve_reference with anchored vs non-anchored dotted names.
Ensure _by_path handles probes without leading './' correctly.

handoff.purpose: Provides functions for extracting code references from prose and resolving them against the repository source tree.

symbols.name: _strip_code_blocks
symbols.note: Strips fenced code blocks and indented code lines from text, returns prose lines and count of dropped lines.

symbols.name: extract_references
symbols.note: Extracts candidate code references from prose text using regex patterns; returns unresolved references and dropped line count.

symbols.name: _EXCLUDED_DIRS
symbols.note: Frozenset of directory names excluded from suffix index.

symbols.name: _suffix_index
symbols.note: Builds a mapping from every path suffix to all Python files ending with that suffix, excluding certain directories.

symbols.name: _module_file
symbols.note: Resolves a module path (as tuple of parts) to an actual file, optionally using suffix index for partial matches.

symbols.name: _collect_names
symbols.note: Collects top-level names, class members, and detects dynamic namespace from AST body.

symbols.name: _parse_cache
symbols.note: Parses a Python file into AST, extracts names via _collect_names, caches result.

symbols.name: resolve_reference
symbols.note: Resolves a Reference against the repository source tree, determining its state (resolving/skipped) and why.

claims.text: A suffix resolves ONLY when exactly one module ends with it. Ambiguity is the absent-module case: two files named index.py mean this module cannot tell which one the sentence is about, and guessing would manufacture a finding against a file the author never mentioned.
claims.why: In _suffix_index, the return dict maps suffix to list of files; in _module_file and _by_path, hits are only used if len(hits)==1, enforcing uniqueness.

claims.text: Measured: 370 of 374 skipped references were relative like this, so a root-anchored resolver was declining to check the overwhelming majority of the corpus and reporting a confident zero.
claims.why: This claim references measurements not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Walks into module-level if/try bodies, because a conditional or guarded import is a normal way to define a public name and missing it would manufacture a false 'this symbol does not exist'.
claims.why: The function explicitly handles ast.If and ast.Try nodes, recursing into their bodies and also into orelse, finalbody, and handlers.

claims.text: The precondition for judging AT ALL is that the module resolves. A reference whose module is absent is 'skipped' -- see the module docstring on why that is the entire false-positive filter.
claims.why: If module is None after resolution attempts, the function returns a Reference with state 'skipped' and a why message indicating no module found.

claims.text: A trailing call suffix is how prose names a function; it is not part of the name.
claims.why: In extract_references, probe = raw[:-2].strip() if raw.endswith('()') else raw, stripping the '()' suffix.

claims.text: ANCHORED only if the dotted prefix is a real module path from the repo root. ... a bare 'vendors' resolved through the suffix index is not -- see the note on _suffix_index and the measured false positives below.
claims.why: The variable 'anchored' is set to True only if _module_file(root, parts[:n], None) is not None, meaning the module resolves without suffix index.

claims.text: Measured: the first version of this file called TWO methods missing -- ollama.py::_run_rewrite (line 423) and a test at line 183 -- because it looked only at module scope. Accepting any class member is deliberately LOOSE: it can only turn a finding into a non-finding, which is the direction a checker that dispatches work is allowed to be wrong in.
claims.where: resolve_reference, after checking head not in names
claims.why: This claim references measurements and specific line numbers not present in this chunk.

observations.what: _strip_code_blocks uses fence token of first three characters; may not match fences with different token lengths.
_suffix_index builds index from all .py files under root, which may be large; no caching beyond the module.
_collect_names treats star imports and __getattr__ as dynamic, causing any reference to such module to be skipped.
resolve_reference uses _by_path with lstrip('./') but probe may not have leading './'; may miss suffix matches.
resolve_reference for dotted names uses longest module prefix; anchored flag only set if direct _module_file succeeds.
